learning_objective: 🎯 Discover the mathematical beauty of number patterns with a constant difference, find any future term, and calculate massive sums instantly!

main_concepts.simple_explanation: An AP is a list of numbers where each term is obtained by adding a fixed number (positive, negative, or zero) to the preceding term. This fixed number is the 'common difference' (d).
If 'a' is the first term and 'd' is the common difference, the AP looks like this: a, a+d, a+2d, a+3d, ...
To find any term in the sequence without writing it all out, use the formula: an = a + (n-1)d. (Here, an is the nth term, and n is the position).
To add up the first n terms quickly, use the formula: Sn = n/2 × [2a + (n-1)d]. If you know the last term (l), you can use the shorter formula: Sn = n/2 × [a + l].

fun_activity.title: 🏦 The Piggy Bank Challenge
fun_activity.instructions: Imagine you save ₹10 on day 1, ₹15 on day 2, ₹20 on day 3, and so on. This is an AP! (a=10, d=5). Use the Sn formula to calculate how much money you will have after 30 days!

exam_tips: 📌 Always check if a sequence is an AP by verifying that (a2 - a1) is exactly equal to (a3 - a2).
📌 Be careful with the common difference 'd'; it can be negative! If the sequence is decreasing (e.g., 10, 7, 4...), d is -3, not 3.
📌 If three numbers in an AP are unknown, assume them to be (a-d), a, (a+d). This makes addition calculations much easier as 'd' cancels out.
quick_recap: ⭐ The common difference 'd' is found by subtracting the current term from the next term (d = a_k+1 - a_k).
⭐ The nth term formula acts as a time machine to jump directly to any position in the sequence.
⭐ The sum formula was famously figured out by mathematician Carl Friedrich Gauss when he was just a schoolboy!
